design_analysis: Include conduct expectations, protected reporting, investigation and consistent consequences; reconcile employee and contractor coverage.
mapping_limit: Acknowledgment alone does not demonstrate tone, investigations or sanctions.

design_analysis: Document governing-body oversight, relevant expertise, independence and review of management's control performance.
mapping_limit: Charter existence does not establish independent challenge or exercised oversight.

design_analysis: Connect corporate authority, service ownership, site operators and supplier escalation; show how responsibilities are communicated.
mapping_limit: Role labels are not appointments; provider duties need enforceable allocation.

design_analysis: Define required skills, screening, training, staffing capacity and succession for service and recovery roles.
mapping_limit: Screening and qualifications alone omit development, retention and backup coverage.

design_analysis: Tie assigned control duties to performance review, incentives, excessive-pressure assessment and corrective consequences.
mapping_limit: A control-owner list and self-assessment omit performance accountability.

design_analysis: Reconcile information used by controls to reliable source populations, asset/data-flow inventories, classification and location.
mapping_limit: Export integrity alone omits whether the information is relevant, timely and complete.

design_analysis: Communicate objectives, system boundaries, changed responsibilities and confidential issue-reporting routes to staff and governance.
mapping_limit: Policy publication alone omits understanding, upward reporting and change communications.

design_analysis: Give customers and providers accurate service boundaries, commitments, responsibilities and incident/contact routes; route incoming concerns.
mapping_limit: Contract clauses alone omit two-way communications and operational notices.

design_analysis: Translate accepted security, availability and confidentiality commitments into specific risk objectives and tolerances.
mapping_limit: A risk appetite document needs service-specific measures and resource implications.

design_analysis: Analyze threats and vulnerabilities across the service, corporate dependencies and providers; assign treatments for significant risks.
mapping_limit: A register entry needs supported analysis, affected assets and response ownership.

design_analysis: Include malicious insiders, management override, misuse of access, incentives and dishonest reporting in fraud scenarios.
mapping_limit: Financial fraud analysis alone misses information-system abuse.

design_analysis: Reassess changes in service model, leadership, providers, technology, obligations and threats.
mapping_limit: Project review alone misses external change and emerging threats.

design_analysis: Combine ongoing monitoring with objective separate evaluations; adjust scope and cadence to risk and change.
mapping_limit: Self-certification is management monitoring; independent assurance needs separate competence and authority.

design_analysis: Evaluate deficiencies, notify responsible management/governance and verify corrective action effectiveness.
mapping_limit: Closing a ticket without independent validation is insufficient.

design_analysis: Select preventive/detective controls from service risk; document incompatible duties and compensating review.
mapping_limit: A registry mapping does not establish a suitably designed activity.

design_analysis: Connect infrastructure, access and development controls to the technologies actually supporting the service.
mapping_limit: Generic minimum standards need platform-specific technical design and deployed configuration evidence.

design_analysis: Translate policy into named execution roles, triggers, corrective actions and periodically updated procedures.
mapping_limit: A published policy is insufficient without evidence of execution.

design_analysis: Specify identities, authentication, privileged paths, resource authorization, segmentation and protection of credentials and cryptographic keys.
mapping_limit: IAM lifecycle mappings need AUTH-TECH and CRYPTO-TRANSFER design supplements.

design_analysis: Verify identity and authorization before issuing access; reconcile all identity stores and revoke access when authorization ends.
mapping_limit: Directory controls need local accounts, customer administration and supplier access coverage.

design_analysis: Authorize rights by job duties and least privilege; review conflicts and changed access needs.
mapping_limit: Additions alone omit removals, segregation conflicts and privileged exceptions.

design_analysis: Define approved zones, credentials, visitors, escort, access review and removal at both sites and provider facilities.
mapping_limit: Generic security architecture needs PHYSICAL-SITE supplement and provider evidence.

design_analysis: Keep devices and media protected until data/software are removed or rendered unrecoverable under the approved disposition.
mapping_limit: Asset retirement status alone is not verified sanitization.

design_analysis: Protect external paths using approved ingress/egress rules, strong authentication and restricted administrative channels.
mapping_limit: Network policy alone needs concrete configurations and external-path testing.

design_analysis: Authorize transfers and removals; protect channels, media and endpoints; record encryption and key responsibilities.
mapping_limit: CRYPTO-TRANSFER supplement must address exported data and removable media as well as replication.

design_analysis: Restrict software installation, detect unauthorized changes and malicious code, and handle externally introduced files.
mapping_limit: Endpoint baseline alone requires effective enforcement, alert handling and exceptions.

design_analysis: Detect configuration drift, unknown components and vulnerabilities across the full asset population.
mapping_limit: A scanner list omits discovery reconciliation and actionable drift management.

design_analysis: Monitor anomalies and detection-system health; tune detection to service risks and review collection gaps.
mapping_limit: Log retention alone does not demonstrate useful detection or functioning collection.

design_analysis: Triage events against service objectives and confidentiality impact; preserve dismissals and incident classifications.
mapping_limit: An incident ticket alone omits impact analysis and classification completeness.

design_analysis: Exercise command, containment, mitigation, communication, eradication and return to service; handle legal notice duties separately.
mapping_limit: A runbook needs tested contacts, authority, upstream notice clocks and decision evidence.

design_analysis: Recover affected services, communicate status, analyze causes and validate preventive improvements and recovery plans.
mapping_limit: A successful restore alone omits recurrence prevention and lessons learned.

design_analysis: Control requirements, design, testing, approval, release and emergency changes across code, configuration, infrastructure and data.
mapping_limit: Repository review alone misses runtime reconciliation, purchased systems and emergency work.

design_analysis: Treat disruption risks across primary/recovery sites and critical suppliers; consider risk-transfer options as part of management's analysis.
mapping_limit: A BIA identifies impact but does not itself implement mitigation; insurance is not presumed mandatory.

design_analysis: Tier suppliers, assess scope and exceptions, establish duties, monitor performance and plan exit.
mapping_limit: A provider assurance report does not automatically cover customer responsibilities or our site dependencies.

design_analysis: Measure current load, forecast average/peak demand and trigger capacity changes against accepted service objectives at both sites.
mapping_limit: CAPACITY supplement is required; a BIA alone cannot demonstrate available recovery headroom.

design_analysis: Address environmental threats, monitored protection, resilient processing and recoverable off-site backups.
mapping_limit: ENVIRONMENT supplement and provider evidence are needed in addition to backup policy.

design_analysis: Exercise service recovery and verify backup completeness/integrity against accepted recovery objectives.
mapping_limit: Backup job success alone is insufficient; validate usable recovery and dependencies.

design_analysis: Identify confidential data and obligations; control retention and protection against premature destruction throughout its lifecycle.
mapping_limit: Classification alone omits retention execution and protected recovery copies.

design_analysis: Identify data eligible for destruction and verify deletion across media, providers and backup lifecycle while respecting holds.
mapping_limit: A retention schedule alone omits execution and documented residual copies.

design_analysis: Draft the services offered, intended customers and relevant service operations; tie statements to the proposed service inventory.
mapping_limit: Use proposed wording until actual service facts and management ownership are supplied.

design_analysis: List principal service commitments and system requirements, their origins and relationship to the selected categories.
mapping_limit: Do not invent customer SLAs, RTO/RPO or contractual obligations.

design_analysis: Describe infrastructure, software, people, procedures and data with boundaries and data flows, including corporate and recovery dependencies.
mapping_limit: Inventory labels alone omit how components interact and which parties operate them.

design_analysis: Maintain the incident population and assess incidents affecting achievement of service commitments during the reporting period.
mapping_limit: No supplied incidents is not evidence that no material incidents occurred.

design_analysis: Explain selected criteria and controls sufficient for users to understand the design and relevant period operation.
mapping_limit: Candidate mappings must not be described as implemented controls.

design_analysis: Identify customer actions necessary with our controls to meet commitments, and explain their interaction.
mapping_limit: Do not label every customer duty a complementary user-entity control or assume execution.

design_analysis: Identify subservice organizations, functions, scope treatment and complementary dependencies; reconcile report coverage.
mapping_limit: Carve-out/inclusive treatment requires engagement facts and examiner agreement; supplier opinions are not inherited.

design_analysis: Explain any criterion determined irrelevant to the system and its factual basis.
mapping_limit: Owner category selection is not approval of individual exclusions.

design_analysis: Maintain changes relevant to the system description and service commitments across the period.
mapping_limit: A release list must include organizational, supplier and infrastructure changes and their effects.
